title: From source drift to a trusted release
summary: A human-gated workflow for reviewing source changes, updating affected learning content, releasing an approval-bound revision, monitoring it, and retaining rollback evidence.
description: This lesson presents a complete governance model. A bounded operator observation supplied for this lesson and dated 2026-09-20 reports that a monthly corpus-inspection job was configured and that its retained 2026-09-15 execution succeeded. The observed runtime used a pinned canonical corpus and produced classified findings. That observation does not establish automatic provider-source comparison, complete upstream revalidation, human approval, publication, live acceptance, or deployment of this lesson. Each capability requires its own evidence.
safetyNotice: This browser-only lesson does not call an Orchard control plane, approve or publish a release, store decisions, monitor production, or perform network requests. Orchard records and transitions are fictional teaching fixtures. A review-due date is an administrative trigger, not proof of drift. A fetch failure or missing citation establishes an evidence gap, not freshness or staleness. A source change requires comparison before anyone concludes that a dependent claim is incorrect.
diagramLabel: Interactive native workflow from an approved source registry through scheduled review, impact mapping, proposal, automated checks, human approval, versioned release, monitoring, and rollback.
textAlternativeLabel: Read the complete workflow as text
textAlternative: Approved source registry leads to scheduled detection and review, then impact mapping, then an evidence-linked proposal. Automated factuality, citation, consistency, and assessment checks either fail and return the proposal for correction or pass to human preview. Human review either requests a revision and returns it for renewed checks or approves an exact revision for release. Monitoring after release either reports a healthy result and returns to routine registry review or identifies a confirmed regression. A regression produces an incident record, restores a bounded known-good release, and returns to the registry with unresolved source-currency work still visible.
practiceInstructions: Each case supplies all facts needed for its decision. Choose an action and read the causal feedback. The solution remains hidden until that case has been attempted. Completion is earned only after all three cases have been solved. Retry clears the selected answer for one case. Reset clears every selection, solution, and completion result.
retryAnnouncement: Case ready for another attempt. The prior submission remains counted.
resetAnnouncement: All practice progress and solutions have been reset.
sourcesIntroduction: These public references provide background on AI risk management, provenance, and change-control practices. They do not substantiate the fictional Orchard records or the supplied private operator observation.
takeaways: Automate inspection and impact mapping without treating an automated finding as permission to publish.
Bind approval to the exact checked revision and release inventory. A later edit requires renewed checks and approval.
Treat review dates, source changes, claim correctness, fetch failures, and missing evidence as different states.
A rollback can restore known-good behavior without making older affected content current under newer evidence.
Retain failed checks, requested revisions, approvals, release inventories, incidents, and rollback boundaries.

nodes.heading: Approved source registry
nodes.description: Record the approved source identity, captured evidence, review policy, and provenance. A due date schedules review but does not decide whether source content changed.

nodes.heading: Scheduled detection and review
nodes.description: Inspect available canonical-corpus evidence and classify outcomes precisely. Changed evidence, unavailable evidence, unchanged evidence, and review due are separate results.

nodes.heading: Impact map
nodes.description: Trace a changed source statement to every claim, example, answer key, distractor explanation, and check that depends on it. Then decide whether the change makes each item incorrect.

nodes.heading: Evidence-linked proposal
nodes.description: Draft exact replacement text and assessment changes. Keep the previous text, new evidence, rationale, wrong-option feedback, and revision identity together.

nodes.heading: Automated checks
nodes.description: Run factuality, citation-presence, internal-consistency, and assessment checks. Retain failures. Every corrected or human-revised object must be checked as its own revision.

nodes.heading: Human preview and approval
nodes.description: A reviewer previews a checked revision, requests a bounded revision or approves that exact immutable revision. A requested revision returns through checks. Approval does not transfer to later edits.

nodes.heading: Versioned release and audit record
nodes.description: Publish only a checked revision with a matching approval. Record every included claim, example, prompt, option, answer key, and feedback item.

nodes.heading: Monitor quality and freshness
nodes.description: Observe post-release behavior. A healthy result returns to routine registry review. A confirmed regression follows the rollback branch. Neither result replaces source review.

nodes.heading: Rollback with recorded reason
nodes.description: Restore only the known-good scope identified by the rollback manifest. Retain the failed release and incident, and withhold affected material that is obsolete under newer source evidence.

artifacts.label: Registry fixture
artifacts.title: ORCH-SRC-17, a noncryptographic record ID
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL RECORD
Approved source: Orchard Model Guide, section 4.2, “Batch limits”
Previous capture date: 2026-07-10
Previous source record ID: ORCH-CAP-0710-A, noncryptographic
Previous excerpt: “A batch may contain up to 100 items.”
Review-due date: 2026-09-15
Policy result: Review is due. This result alone says nothing about drift or claim correctness.

artifacts.label: Bounded status
artifacts.title: What the supplied observation reports as of 2026-09-20
artifacts.body: A supplied read-only operator observation reports a configured monthly corpus-inspection job and a retained execution from 2026-09-15 06:00:00Z through 06:05:40Z marked Succeeded. The inspected runtime materialized a pinned canonical corpus, enumerated items, submitted canonical-source content for structured inspection, and produced classified findings. The inspected call included no web-search or source-fetch tool. This supports only the bounded statement that scheduled corpus inspection was observed. It does not establish provider-source byte comparison, revalidation of every upstream byte, human approval, publication, live acceptance, or deployment of this lesson.

artifacts.label: Changed-source fixture
artifacts.title: Comparison record ORCH-CMP-0915-B
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL RECORD
New capture date: 2026-09-14
New source record ID: ORCH-CAP-0914-B, noncryptographic
New excerpt: “A batch may contain up to 80 items. Requests containing more than 80 items are rejected before processing.”
Comparison decision: The captured statement changed from 100 to 80.
Substantive decision: The lesson claim “up to 100 items” conflicts with the supplied new excerpt and requires revision.
No cryptographic digest is claimed for these fixture IDs.

artifacts.label: Classification rule
artifacts.title: Do not infer freshness from missing evidence
artifacts.body: If the 2026-09-14 capture had failed, the exact decision would be “evidence unavailable; investigate and preserve the last verified capture.” It would not be “source changed,” “source unchanged,” “lesson stale,” or “lesson fresh.” A missing citation establishes that required support is absent. It does not by itself establish that the claim is false.

artifacts.label: Impact record
artifacts.title: ORCH-IMPACT-23
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL DEPENDENCIES
Affected claim: “Orchard accepts batches containing up to 100 items.”
Affected worked example: “A batch of 90 items is accepted.”
Previous assessment prompt: “Under the previous 100-item limit, which is the largest accepted batch among 80, 90, and 100 items?”
Previous answer key: 100 items.
Required new assessment prompt: “Using the supplied 2026-09-14 excerpt, which request is within the stated batch limit?”
Required new answer key: 80 items.
Required new wrong-option feedback for 90: 90 exceeds the stated limit of 80 by 10 items.
Required new wrong-option feedback for 100: 100 is the former limit and exceeds the new stated limit of 80 by 20 items.
Unaffected claim: “A rejected request is not processed.”
Causal conclusion: The numerical change makes the old claim, example, answer key, and old distractor explanations incorrect. The rejection claim remains supported by the new excerpt.

artifacts.label: Proposal revision PR-01
artifacts.title: Initial evidence-linked revision
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL EXACT TEXT
Replace claim with: “Orchard accepts batches containing up to 80 items.”
Replace worked example with: “A batch of 80 items is accepted; a batch of 81 items is rejected before processing.”
Replace assessment prompt with: “Which request is within the stated limit: 80, 90, or 100 items?”
Proposed answer key: 80 items.
Wrong-option feedback for 90: “90 exceeds the 80-item limit.”
Wrong-option feedback for 100: “100 was the previous limit and exceeds the 80-item limit.”
Evidence: ORCH-CAP-0914-B.
Revision record: PR-01.

artifacts.label: Proposal revisions PR-02 and PR-03
artifacts.title: Automated correction followed by human revision
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL REVISION HISTORY
PR-02 corrected the failed citation-date check:
Claim: “Under the Orchard Model Guide captured on 2026-09-14, a batch may contain up to 80 items; a request above 80 items is rejected before processing.”
Worked example: “A request with 80 items is within the stated limit. A request with 81 items exceeds the limit and is rejected before processing.”
Assessment: “Using the supplied 2026-09-14 excerpt, which request is within the stated batch limit?”
Options: “80 items”; “90 items”; “100 items”.
Answer key: “80 items”.

PR-03 applied the later human request without changing the claim, options, or key:
Feedback for 80: “Correct. 80 is exactly the maximum stated in the supplied excerpt.”
Feedback for 90: “Incorrect. 90 exceeds the stated limit of 80 by 10 items, so the request is rejected before processing.”
Feedback for 100: “Incorrect. 100 is the former limit. It exceeds the supplied 2026-09-14 limit of 80 by 20 items.”
Evidence for both revisions: ORCH-CAP-0914-B.

artifacts.label: Retained failed check
artifacts.title: CHECK-PR01-01 failed
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL RESULT
Input revision: PR-01
Check: citation-date specificity
Expected: A date-bounded statement because the proposal relies on a captured fictional excerpt.
Observed: The claim said “Orchard accepts” without identifying the 2026-09-14 capture.
Decision: FAIL. Return PR-01 to proposal.
Correction required: Create a new revision that adds the evidence date without changing the 80-item answer key.

artifacts.label: Retained recheck records
artifacts.title: CHECK-PR02-02 and CHECK-PR03-03
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL RESULTS
CHECK-PR02-02 input revision: PR-02
Citation-date check: PASS.
Claim-to-excerpt check: PASS.
Worked-example check: PASS.
Assessment-key check: PASS.
Decision: Send checked PR-02 to human preview.

CHECK-PR03-03 input revision: PR-03
Revision-difference check: PASS. The added feedback matches the 80-item limit and preserves the options and key.
Wrong-option feedback check: PASS. Feedback for 90 and 100 explains each error against the new limit.
Decision: PR-03 is checked and may be considered for approval.
No score, ranking, or probabilistic factuality claim is asserted.

artifacts.label: Human revision record
artifacts.title: REVIEW-PR02-07
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL DECISION
Previewed revision: PR-02
Prerequisite: CHECK-PR02-02 passed for PR-02.
Decision: REVISE
Bounded request: “Add causal feedback for each option. Explain that 90 is 10 above the new limit and that 100 is the former limit and 20 above the new limit. Do not alter the prompt, options, keyed value, claim, or evidence identity.”
Resolution: PR-03 applies that request. Because PR-03 is a distinct revision, it returns to automated checks before approval. The request remains retained beside the later check and approval.

artifacts.label: Approval record
artifacts.title: APPROVAL-PR03-09
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL DECISION
Approved revision: PR-03
Approved check record: CHECK-PR03-03
Approved inventory candidate: claim, worked example, assessment prompt, options, answer key, and option-specific feedback listed in PR-03.
Binding rule: Approval applies only to PR-03. Editing any approved text, evidence link, option, answer key, or feedback creates another revision that must be checked and approved again.

artifacts.label: Release manifest
artifacts.title: ORCH-REL-2026-09-16-1
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL RELEASE
Released revision: PR-03
Approval: APPROVAL-PR03-09
Check record: CHECK-PR03-03
Included items: lesson claim CLM-17; worked example EX-17; assessment ASMT-17 prompt; options 80, 90, and 100; answer key 80; correct feedback for 80; revised wrong-option feedback for 90 and 100; evidence record ORCH-CAP-0914-B.
Feedback for 90: 90 exceeds 80 by 10 and is rejected before processing.
Feedback for 100: 100 is the former limit, exceeds 80 by 20, and is rejected before processing.
Previous operationally known-good release: ORCH-REL-2026-08-01-3.
Decision: Publish PR-03 only because its revision, check, approval, and inventory identities match.

artifacts.label: Monitoring incident
artifacts.title: ORCH-INC-44
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL OBSERVATION
Release under observation: ORCH-REL-2026-09-16-1
Canary fixture input: Select “80 items” for ASMT-17.
Expected under PR-03: Accepted as correct.
Observed: The rendered canary marked “80 items” incorrect because a packaging defect loaded the previous key “100 items.”
Decision: Confirmed release regression. This is not source drift. Stop promotion, preserve the incident, and apply the bounded rollback policy.

artifacts.label: Rollback manifest
artifacts.title: ORCH-RB-44
artifacts.body:
FICTIONAL ROLLBACK
Incident retained: ORCH-INC-44
Failed release retained for diagnosis: ORCH-REL-2026-09-16-1
Operational package restored: ORCH-REL-2026-08-01-3
Reason: ASMT-17 in the September package loaded the previous answer key and failed the deterministic canary.
Safe restoration boundary: Restore the previously working application package and unaffected content only.
Source-currency boundary: The August release still contains the obsolete 100-item lesson and assessment. It is not labeled current or correct under ORCH-CAP-0914-B.
Withheld item: ASMT-17 and its affected 100-item lesson content remain unavailable after rollback until a corrected 80-item package is checked, approved, released, and monitored.
Decision: Restore bounded known-good behavior without deleting evidence or silently reintroducing obsolete affected content. Return to the registry with source-currency and corrective packaging work still open.

practiceGroups.title: Case 1: changed fact affects an answer key
practiceGroups.prompt: Supplied inputs: The previous excerpt says “up to 40 tokens.” The new dated excerpt says “up to 32 tokens; larger requests are rejected.” A lesson still says 40, and its assessment keys 40. The new capture is available and its identity is recorded. What is the exact governance decision?
practiceGroups.solution: Map the change to both the lesson claim and answer key, propose 32 with the dated evidence, run checks, and require human approval before release. The changed limit directly contradicts 40, so both dependent items require revision.

practiceGroups.title: Case 2: an edit after approval
practiceGroups.prompt: Supplied inputs: Revision RX-7 passed checks and was approved. Before publication, an editor changes its answer option from “32” to “30,” creating RX-8. No checks or approval mention RX-8. What is the exact decision?
practiceGroups.solution: Block publication of RX-8. Treat it as a new revision, rerun applicable checks, and obtain approval bound to RX-8. Approval of RX-7 cannot authorize changed learner-facing content in RX-8.

practiceGroups.title: Case 3: a post-release regression
practiceGroups.prompt: Supplied inputs: Release NEW-2 was approved and published. A deterministic canary shows that its packaged answer key marks the documented correct option wrong. Release GOOD-1 previously passed that canary, but one affected lesson in GOOD-1 uses an older source limit. The source evidence itself has not changed. What is the exact decision?
practiceGroups.solution: Record a release incident, restore only the known-good operational scope from GOOD-1, retain NEW-2 and the incident, withhold the source-obsolete affected lesson, and open a corrective packaging proposal. The failure is a release regression, while the older lesson remains a separate source-currency issue.

choices.label: Revise the claim and key to 32 through checks and human approval.
choices.feedback: Correct. The supplied new excerpt contradicts the old numerical claim, and the answer key depends on that claim. Both must follow the checked, human-gated release path.

choices.label: Record only that review is due; do not map assessment impact.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. A due date alone would not prove drift, but this case supplies an actual changed excerpt. Ignoring the answer-key dependency would leave a known inconsistency.

choices.label: Keep 40 because a changed source never proves a claim incorrect.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. A source change is not always substantive, but this supplied change directly replaces 40 with 32. The comparison establishes that the old claim and dependent key conflict with the new evidence.

choices.label: Block RX-8, rerun checks, and obtain approval bound to RX-8.
choices.feedback: Correct. The edit changed the approved object. Checks and approval for RX-7 do not transfer to RX-8.

choices.label: Publish RX-8 because RX-7 was already approved.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Publishing RX-8 would bypass approval binding. The changed option could alter assessment validity and was never checked or approved as RX-8.

choices.label: Relabel RX-8 as RX-7 so the existing approval still matches.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Relabeling would conceal the post-approval edit and break the audit trail rather than establish authorization.

choices.label: Restore the safe scope of GOOD-1, withhold its obsolete affected lesson, and retain all incident evidence.
choices.feedback: Correct. The canary establishes a packaging regression. A bounded rollback limits harm, while withholding the source-obsolete lesson prevents the rollback from falsely presenting old affected content as current.

choices.label: Delete NEW-2 and its monitoring evidence, then restore every part of GOOD-1.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Deleting the failed release removes evidence needed for diagnosis and audit. Restoring every part of GOOD-1 would also reintroduce affected content known to be obsolete under newer evidence.

choices.label: Mark the source as newly changed and wait for scheduled review.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. The source did not change during this incident. Waiting would misclassify a confirmed packaging regression and leave incorrect behavior active.

simulator.heading: Browser-only release-state exercise
simulator.instructions: Use the actions to explore precondition-gated paths. PR-01 must retain its failed check. PR-02 can reach human preview only after correction and checks. Human revision creates PR-03 and requires a new check. A separate branch shows that editing approved PR-02 into PR-03 invalidates the old approval. A matching publication can then reach either a healthy monitoring result or a regression and bounded rollback. Actions with unmet preconditions do not change state.
simulator.resetAnnouncement: State exercise reset to unchecked PR-01.
simulator.completedLabel: Exercise complete: bounded rollback evidence retained

states.label: PR-02 checks passed; awaiting human decision
Human revision requested on checked PR-02
PR-03 exists; no PR-02 approval applies
PR-02 approved; approval binds only PR-02
PR-03 approved; approval binds only PR-03
PR-02 published with matching PR-02 approval
PR-03 published with matching PR-03 approval
PR-02 monitored healthy; routine review resumes
PR-03 monitored healthy; routine review resumes
PR-02 release rolled back within recorded boundaries
PR-03 release rolled back within recorded boundaries

actions.label: Run checks on PR-01
actions.successFeedback: CHECK-PR01-01 fails because PR-01 omits the evidence date. The failure is retained and publication remains blocked.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-01 can be checked only while PR-01 is the current unchecked proposal.

actions.label: Correct PR-01 as PR-02
actions.successFeedback: PR-02 adds the 2026-09-14 evidence date and preserves the 80-item key. PR-02 still requires its own checks.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-02 can be created through this action only after the retained PR-01 failure identifies the correction.

actions.label: Run checks on PR-02
actions.successFeedback: CHECK-PR02-02 passes for PR-02. The checked identity is PR-02, and human preview is now permitted.
actions.blockedFeedback: This action requires corrected, unchecked PR-02.

actions.label: Request causal feedback in human preview
actions.successFeedback: The reviewer requests option-specific causal feedback. PR-02 is not approved. Applying the request must create a new revision.
actions.blockedFeedback: A human revision request requires checked PR-02 at human preview.

actions.label: Apply the human revision as PR-03
actions.successFeedback: PR-03 adds the requested feedback. It is a distinct unchecked revision and cannot reuse any PR-02 check or approval.
actions.blockedFeedback: This human-revision action requires a retained revision request on PR-02.

actions.label: Approve checked PR-02
actions.successFeedback: Approval is bound to checked PR-02. It authorizes only unchanged PR-02.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-02 approval requires checked PR-02. It cannot approve PR-01 or PR-03.

actions.label: Edit approved PR-02 to create PR-03
actions.successFeedback: The edit creates PR-03. PR-02 approval does not authorize PR-03, so publication is blocked until PR-03 is checked and approved.
actions.blockedFeedback: This post-approval edit demonstration requires approved PR-02.

actions.label: Run checks on PR-03
actions.successFeedback: CHECK-PR03-03 passes for PR-03. The state retains PR-03 identity, and human approval is still required.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-03 can be checked only while unchecked PR-03 is current.

actions.label: Approve checked PR-03
actions.successFeedback: APPROVAL-PR03-09 is bound to checked PR-03. It does not revive or reuse PR-02 approval.

actions.label: Publish approval-bound PR-02
actions.successFeedback: PR-02 is simulated as published with matching PR-02 approval. No external publication occurred.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-02 publication requires current, unchanged, approved PR-02.

actions.label: Publish approval-bound PR-03
actions.successFeedback: PR-03 is simulated as published with matching PR-03 checks, approval, and inventory. No external publication occurred.
actions.blockedFeedback: PR-03 publication requires current, unchanged, approved PR-03. PR-02 approval is insufficient.

actions.label: Record a healthy PR-02 canary
actions.successFeedback: The supplied healthy branch is recorded for published PR-02. Routine registry review resumes, but monitoring does not prove future freshness.
actions.blockedFeedback: A healthy PR-02 result requires published PR-02.

actions.label: Record a healthy PR-03 canary
actions.successFeedback: The supplied healthy branch is recorded for published PR-03. Routine registry review resumes, but monitoring does not prove future freshness.
actions.blockedFeedback: A healthy PR-03 result requires published PR-03.

actions.label: Record a PR-02 regression
actions.successFeedback: A deterministic canary records a PR-02 release regression. Rollback now requires a bounded manifest.
actions.blockedFeedback: A PR-02 regression can be recorded only for published PR-02.

actions.label: Record the supplied PR-03 regression
actions.successFeedback: The canary records that packaged PR-03 rejects the keyed option 80. This is a release regression, not source drift.
actions.blockedFeedback: The supplied PR-03 regression requires published PR-03.

actions.label: Apply a bounded PR-02 rollback
actions.successFeedback: The safe operational scope is restored, obsolete affected content is withheld, and the PR-02 release and incident remain recorded.
actions.blockedFeedback: A PR-02 rollback requires a confirmed PR-02 regression.

actions.label: Apply the bounded PR-03 rollback
actions.successFeedback: The safe operational scope is restored. The obsolete August assessment remains withheld, and the failed PR-03 release and incident remain recorded.
actions.blockedFeedback: A PR-03 rollback requires the supplied confirmed PR-03 regression.
